newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs could see retreat before next leap.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs could see retreat before next leap.

text.p: Confidence and bullishness will continue to characterise the tone on the Belgian bond market this week, dealers said on Monday, but they were split on the chances of a temporary setback before further price gains.

A positive tone elsewhere helped the market advance modestly on Monday, but volumes were becalmed with some end-investors absent due to Spring school holidays and others scaling back activity to take account of the reduced number of players.
One trader said prices would edge down until the conclusion of the U.S. refunding auctions on Thursday when the uptrend would resume. "Everybody is full of confidence," he said.
"Even if there were a crash the Belgian market would still hold up...everybody is bullish, bullish, bullish," he said.

However, there were arguments for contrarians too. "I am sceptical," he said, indicating that the continued strength of the U.S. economy would of necessity trigger an increase in short-term rates and bring about a market correction.
"That makes me tend towards short positions," he said.

Another noted that the undertone was positive. "You should have long positions rather than short ones...with a steep (yield) curve you are better off with longs," he said, predicting a further gradual rise in prices.

He noted the whole of the Belgian yield curve was expensive relative to its German counterpart and foresaw some spread widening. The 10-year OLO yield premium over Bunds was at seven basis points at 1537 GMT, unchanged from Friday's close.
Dealers noted the OLO/Bund spread was currently near the bottom of its near-term range of five to 15 basis points.

Players foresaw no near-term news to break the uptrend. "The market is structurally short...market makers are keen on long paper," said one trader. Another said the steepness of the curve -- with a three-month/10-year spread of 268 bps -- made further flattening trades likely.
He said yields were attractive at the longer end and static at the short end.
"(A yield of) 5.60 (percent) is possible on the 10-year," said the first trader, noting earlier today the key Bund future had broken above 102.62, giving the Belgian market impetus.
He said the frontmonth Bund future now had room to rise to 103.00, which equalled a yield of 5.65 percent on the closely linked 10-year benchmark 2007 OLO.
The OLO yielded 5.67 percent at 1550 GMT, down from 5.69 at the close on Friday. March Bunds were up 0.14 at 102.68, but off an intraday high at 102.72.
March OLO futures rose 0.14 at 122.64 after hitting 122.67, a contract high.

Dealers said there was no talk of the market reaching overbought levels. "There is scope for further gains...there are no figures to give the market an impetus until Friday's U.S. PPI numbers...trade will be quiet until then," said one.

January producer prices are forecast to show inflationary pressure year-on-year and at the ex food and energy level. But coupled with Friday's January capacity use and industrial output data -- forecast on the soft side -- the numbers should not spark major inflation concerns and leave the uptrend intact.
